title: Prefetch Oncall Hub and Annotated Autotriage Bundles
author: Evelyn Chu
description:
Motivation: on-call handoffs and first-responder triage often spend several minutes fetching relevant telemetry and assembling playbooks. This PR introduces an "oncall prefetch hub" (hublet) plus a mechanism to produce small, annotated autotriage bundles that can be cached per-service and attached to incidents automatically. The goal is to reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to mitigate (MTTM) by delivering compact, precomputed diagnostic snapshots and ranked playbook steps to responders immediately when an alert fires.

What this change does: adds a lightweight hublet service in slo-toolkit that: (1) continuously seeds telemetry snapshots for high-risk routes using rationalized sampling policies, (2) compiles annotated autotriage bundles (sanitized logs, top traces, relevant kpi deltas, suggested runbook steps with quick commands), and (3) exposes a small API used by incident-bot to attach a bundle to a new incident or to provide a suggested-playbook link in Slack/PagerDuty messages. Bundles are intentionally compact (<= 256KB) and include provenance metadata and an integrity hash.

Design highlights: sampling policies are policy-driven (configurable per-service via YAML), with decay windows to avoid repeated heavy capture during ongoing incidents; sanitization hooks remove PII/keys using existing sanitizers; caching TTLs are conservative (default 5m) and can be overridden by service tier. Attachments are only created for alerts that match selectors to avoid noise. The hublet exposes a CLI (sloctl bundle generate) for on-demand bundle creation and a background worker that runs captures and bundle builds.

Backward compatibility and rollout: incident-bot integration is opt-in via a feature flag `incident_prefetch` in the incident-bot config. Rollout plan: enable for small set of non-sensitive services for 48-hour dogfood, monitor bundle-attached frequency and initial responder feedback, then expand by service. The feature is reversible: disabling the flag stops attachments; bundles remain in cache until TTL expires.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for sampler logic and sanitizers, integration test that simulates an alert -> bundle attach flow, and an end-to-end smoke test that exercises Slack message rendering with bundle link. Load test: lightweight capture path was run at 200 rps against simulated traces (no real customer data).

Observability: added metrics: slo_prefetch.bundle_build_duration_seconds, slo_prefetch.bundles_attached_total, slo_prefetch.sanitizer_dropped_fields_total and a dashboard dashboard/slo-prefetch-bundles. New alerts to watch for rollout: high bundle_build_duration > 5s (P2), sanitizer_error_rate > 1% (P3), unexpected_attach_rate spike.

Security/Privacy: bundles are sanitized; sensitive payloads are dropped or redacted. Access is limited to incident-bot service account via RBAC. We worked with security to ensure KMS keys are not captured in bundles.

Notes: this is intentionally small-scope: hublet is not a full long-term retention store. Future work (separate PRs) will add persistent bundle indexing, ML-based playbook ranking, and richer ephemeral workspace handoff flows.

release_notes: Adds an opt-in oncall prefetch hub and compact annotated autotriage bundles to reduce time-to-first-action for responders. Feature is gated and off by default. See docs/slo-prefetch.md for rollout steps and metrics to monitor.
testing_notes: Unit tests added for sampler, sanitizer. Integration test validates alert->bundle attach. Performed a load run at 200rps against simulated traces in staging; verified sanitizer error rate < 0.1% and average bundle build time 320ms under nominal load.
